lawyer:
AKM Shafiuddin with Binod Kumar Agarwal, Advocates ------ For the Petitioner. 
No one appears ------ For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Azad Hossain (Md) ------ Petitioner
Vs
State  ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J : The petitioner Md Azad Hossain obtained this Rule under section 561A of the Criminal Procedure Code calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Dinajpur to show cause as to why the petitioner arrested and now kept under custody to suffer the sentence passed on 17-6-2001 by the Special Tribunal No. 5, Dinajpur, in Special Tribunal Case No. 41 of 1996 shall not be declared to be illegal and unauthorised since he claimed not to be the convict, Md Abul Kalam Azad, son of Md Nurul Islam, proprietor of “Azad Bastraloy”, who was convicted in absentia under section 258(2) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 and sentenced to suffer RI for 3 (three) years and also to pay a fine of Taka 10,000 in default to suffer RI for 1 (one) year more, and why showing the present petitioner arrested on 5-1-2003 and thereafter issuing custody warrant against the petitioner by order dated 6-1-2003 passed by the Special Tribunal No. 5, Dinajpur in the said Special Tribunal Case No. 41 of 1996 should not be declared to have been passed illegally. 

 2. The petitioner in this Miscellaneous case stated, inter alia, that on 9-4-1991 at about 16-00 hours one Abu Taher, Habildar of BDR, along with others searched one shop namely “Azad Bastraloy” at Goneshtola, Dinajpur Town and allegedly recovered some foreign print sarees as described in the seizure list. Subsequent to the preparation of the seizure list, signatures of the witnesses were obtained but the owner of the shop was not found present at the time of seizure. The informant after depositing the seized articles with the Customs Office lodged the first information report with the Kotwali Police Station, Dinajpur, describing Md Abul Kalam Azad, son of Md Nurul Islam of village Mukundapur PS Kaharol, District Dinajpur as the proprietor of the said “Azad Bastraloy”. After completion of the investigation the nvestigating officer submitted charge-sheet under section 25B(2) of the Special Power Act 1974 against the said Md Abul Kalam Azad, son of Md Nurul Islam of Mukundapur PS Kaharol District Dinajpur showing his present address at Paharpur, PS Kotwali, District Dinajpur, proprietor of “Azad Bastraloy”. Subsequent thereto the case was received by the Special Tribunal for trial wherein charge was framed under section 25B(2) of the Special Powers Act and the accused being absent, the trial was held in absentia and the aforesaid order of conviction and sentence dated 17-6-2001 was passed by the Special Tribunal. 

 3. In the instant case the petitioner Md Azad Hossain stated that he is the son of late Ali Hossain of Village Paharpur, PS Kotwali, District Dinajpur and he along with his son runs a motor cycle shop and whereas the name and address of the convict as appears from the judgment and order of conviction dated 17-6-2001 in Special Tribunal Case No. 41 of 1996 is Md. Abul Kalam Azad son of Md Nurual Islam, Village Mukundaur, PS Kaharol, District Dinajpur presently of Village, Paharpur, PS Kotwali, District Dinajpur. It is further stated that in the first information report and the seizure list the name of the accused has been shown as Md Abul Kalam Azad son of Md Nurul Islam, Village Mukundapur PS Kaharol, District Dinajpur. The present petitioner further stated that at the instance of his rival namely, one Aga Khan and his younger brother Md Azam Khan, sons of late Yusuf Ali Khan, a NGR Case No. 124 of 2002, under section 107 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was started against him wherein the petitioner was intentionally described as Md Azad Hossain @ Abul Kalam Azad. A report was submitted by the local police in that NGR case wherein the name of the accused has been shown as Azad Hossain @ Abul Kalam Azad son of late Ali Hossain @ Nurul Islam of Village Paharpur, PS Kotwali, District Dinajpur and his son Raju of the same address. It is alleged that the said Aga Khan in collusion with the local police managed to submit such report and subsequent thereto the present petitioner has been shown arrested on 5-1-2003 in connection with Special Tribunal Case No. 41 of 1996 in the said NGR Case No. 124 of 2002, The present petitioner filed an application before the Tribunal supported by a copy of his passport issued by the Government of Bangladesh on 16-8-1989, his voter identity card, driving licence, income tax TIN certificate and his son’s SSC certificate and stated that he is not the actual person who has been convicted in the said Special Case No. 41 of 1996, rather he has been falsely described as Md Abul Kalam Azad, son of Md Nurul Islam by his enemy, Aga Khan, who is the petitioner of the said NGR Case No. 124 of 2002 and managed to show him as the convict of the said Special Tribunal Case, only to take revenge as the present petitioner’s daughter Lovely Begum filed Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Case No. 128 of 2001 against her husband Azam Khan, the younger brother of Aga Khan for claiming dowry. Thus the petitioner is innocent and not at all connected or concerned, in any way, with. the said Special Case nor he is Md Abul Kalam Azad, son of Md Nurul Islam, the convict of the said case and prayed for his release. But the learned Judge of the Tribunal without scrutinising the matter as to whether the petitioner is the real convict of the said case and without holding any inquiry to ascertain the identity of the petitioner rejected the application by simply observing that the Tribunal is ‘’functus officio” and allowed the prosecution’s prayer for issuing custody warrant against the present petitioner by his order dated 6-1-2003 challenging which the present Rule has been obtained as the said order amounts to sheer abuse of the process of the Court. 

 5.	Mr AKM Shafiuddin, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that’ the Tribunal erred in law in passing the impugned order dated 6-1-2003 without holding any inquiry in the matter as to the identity of the convict or that of the present petitioner and by simply observing that the tribunal is ‘’functus officio”, rejected the petition. He further submits that all the documents including the first information report, charge-sheet and seizure list show that one Md Abul Kalam Azad, son of Md Nurul Islam of Village, Mukundapur PS Kaharol, District Dinajpur, proprietor of “Azad Bastraloy” was put on trial under section 25(B) of the Special Powers Act in Special Tribunal Case No. 41 of 1996 and the trial being held in absentia the accused was found guilty of the offence charged against him and was convicted and sentenced to suffer RI for 3 (three) years with a fine of Taka. 10,000 in default to suffer RI for 1 (one) year more and whereas the present petitioner not being the same person as evident from the documents produced by him before the Tribunal has been kept behind the bars by the Tribunal without any such offence being committed by him. He submits that the learned Judge neither considered the materials on record nor caused any inquiry to ascertain the facts rather most illegally rejected the petition and passed the order issuing conviction warrant against the petitioner which has caused abuse of the process of the court and, as such, the inherent power of the Court under section 561A of the Code is attracted to secure ends of justice. 

 8. On perusal of the first information report and seizure list it is found that Md Abul Kalam Azad, son of Nurul Islam of Village Mukundapur, PS Kaharol, District. Dinajpur is the person who has been made an accused in the Special Tribunal Case No. 41 of 1996 showing him as the Proprietor of “Azad Bostraloy” of Gonestola, Dinajpur where from the alleged articles were seized. After investigation the police submitted charge-sheet against the said Md Abul Kalam Azad, son of Nurul Islam of Village, Mukundapur, PS Kaharol, District Dinajpur showing to be presently resident of Paharpur, PS Kotwali, Dinajpur but since the said Abul Kalam Azad was not arrested the trial was concluded in his absence and accordingly, the said Md Abul Kalam Azad was convicted and sentenced by judgment and order dated 17-6-2001 passed in Special Tribunal Case No. 41 of 1996. The petitioner has annexed the Non GR case No. 124 of 2002 under section 107 of the Code along with its order sheet wherein it appears that one Md Aga Khan, son of Late Yusuf Ali Khan, is found to have lodged a General Diary on 2-4-2002 with the Kotwali Police Station describing that Md Azad Hossain @ Abul Kalam Azad, son of late Ali Hossain @ Nurul Islam, son Raju describing him as son of Azad Hossain @ Abul Kalam Azad, both of Paharpur, PS Kotwali, District Dinajpur threatened him in presence of witnesses on 1-4-2002 with dire consequences unless the family dispute between his daughter Lovely Begum and her husband Azam Khan, the younger brother of Aga Khan, is settled by compromise on payment of Taka 23 lac, both Aga Khan and his brother Azam Khan would be murdered. Accordingly, the said Aga Khan prayed for protection from the police. On the basis of the said GD entry the aforesaid NGR Case No. 124 of 2002 was started under section 107 of the Criminal Procedure Code. In the said GD the said Aga Khan also stated that his younger brother, Azam Khan is an accused in Nari-o-Shishu Nirjaton Case No. 128 of 2001 corresponding to Kotwali PS Case No. 24(5) 2001 filed by Lovely Begum, daughter of Md Azad Hossain allegedly described as @ Abul Kalam Azad and, as such, the said Azad Hossain @ Md Abul Kalam Azad is threatening them. It appears from order dated 10-7-2002 of the said case that the Investigating Officer in his report stated that the actual name of the accused in the proceeding under section 107 is Md Azad Hossain, son of late Ali Hossain and the accused No.2 is Raju, son of Azad Hossain both residents of Paharpur, PS Kotwali, District Dinajpur and accordingly, he prayed for filing of a supplementary Non First Information Report prosecution in their actual names which the Magistrate found to be reasonable but filed the application subsequent thereto. Subsequently, warrant of arrest was issued against the petitioner wherein accused Md Azad Hossain was arrestted and sent to Court on 30-12-2002 and the other accused Raju having surrendered before the Court was granted bail. In the aforesaid Case No. 124 of 2001 the present petitioner being described as Md Azad Hossain @ Md Abul Kalam Azad was surprisingly shown as the convict of Special Tribunal Case No. 41 of 1996 and the prosecution prayed for showing him arrested in the said Special Tribunal Case as he is the convict therein. The accused petitioner claiming himself to be Md Azad Hossain not Md Abul Kalam Azad and not the actual person who has been convicted and sentenced in the aforesaid Special Case, prayed for bail and in support of his claim he produced several documents. Upon hearing both the parties the Magistrate observed in his order dated 31-12-2002 that whether the accused is actually the convict Abul Kalam Azad of Special Case No. 41 of 1996 is not clear and, as such, rejected his bail prayer and directed the Officer in Charge, Kotwali Police Station to submit a report in the matter before the next date. Subsequently, by order dated 5-1-2003 the Magistrate observed that on the basis of the report of the Officer in Charge of Kotwali Police Station accused Azad Hossain be shown arrested in connection with Special Tribunal Case No. 41 of 1996 without taking into consideration the earlier order dated 10-7-2003 wherein it was observed by the Magistrate that the prosecution’s prayer for filing of a supplementary Non First Information Report Prosecution in the actual names of the accused is reasonable. The learned Magistrate however, allowed the petitioner’s prayer for bail in the said Non GR Case No. 124 of 2001. 

 10. It is true that the learned judge of the Tribunal did not hold any inquiry to ascertain the actual position on the face of the specific assertion of the present petitioner supported by documents filed by him, It is also tru that one Md Abul Kalam Azad, son of Nurul Islam, was convicted in the said Special Tribunal Case and on the face of the petitioner’s specific objection as to his identity that he is not the said Md Abul Kalam Azad, son of Nurul Islam of village Mukundapur, PS Kaharol, Dinajpur rather he is Md Azad Hossain, son of Late Ali Hossain of Paharpur PS Kotwali, Dinajpur the Tribunal ought to have held an inquiry into the matter to secure ends of justice and ought to have come to a definite finding as to the identity of the convict as well as the petitioner to prevent the abuse of the process of the court. The tribunal on the contrary, shrivelled itself and avoided the task of finding the truth by treating itself as “functus officio” and thus shook off its responsibilities without considering that to find out the identify of the real convict there is no necessity at all to re-open the case on merit and, as such, no question of being “functus officio” arises. Had there been a challenge against the judgment of the case then his apprehension could have been appreciated but to ascertain the identity of the actual convict, which is the pertinent question to be decided in this case, it does not, in any way, necessitate interference in the merit of the case. It is the age-old principle followed in dispensing with Criminal Justice that better several guilty persons should escape then one innocent suffers. The learned judge failed to appreciate this aspect of the case and without applying its judicial mind and without adverting to the facts and circumstances of the present case as stated above he mechanically passed the impugned order. In our opinion to that extent the Tribunal acted illegally which caused sheer abuse of the process of the court resulting in failure to secure ends of justice and disregarding that if an innocent is put behind bars leaving aside the real culprit, the faith and confidence in the judiciary will be shattered and the cause of justice will be defeated. 

 11. It has already been stated earlier that at the time of issuance of the Rule the Deputy Commissioner, Dinajpur was directed to hold an inquiry and submit a report in this respect, which has been sent to this Court. We have gone through the said report forwarded by the Deputy Commissioner, Dinajpur and it appears from the report that the learned Magistrate, who was entrusted to hold inquiry examined 18 witnesses and upon considering those evidences and investigating the matter personally opined that no person naming Md Abul Kalam Azad, son of Nurul Islam, proprietor of “Azad Bostraloy” of Goneshtola Dinajpur, who has been convicted in Special Tribunal Case No. 41 of 1996 resides in Village Mokundapur, PS Kaharol, District Dinajpur or at Paharpur PS Kotwali, District Dinajpur nor Md Azad Hossain, son of late Ali Hossain of Paharpur, PS Kotwali, District Dinajpur and the convict of Special Tribunal Case No. 41 of 1996 and Md Abul Kalam Azad, son of Nurul Islam of Mokundapur, Kaharol, Dinajpur Proprietor of “Azad Bostraloy” of Goneshtola, Dinajpur is/are the same person(s). We have carefully examined the said report and also considered the case of the petitioner as made out in his petition as to his identity and on consideration of the materials on record it appears beyond doubt that the report of the Magistrate is based on unimpeachable evidence. We ourselves had to examine this aspect of the case as the same was not done by the learned Tribunal and more so, when the validity of the Order of Conviction depends on the identity of the petitioner. 

 12. Thus, considering the facts and circumstances stated above and upon perusing the report submitted by the Magistrate through the Deputy Commissioner, Dinajpur, we are of the opinion that the present petitioner is a victim of wrong identity who has been put behind bars on a mistaken identity and he is not the same person who has been convicted in Special Tribunal Case No. 41 of 1996 and, as such, the custody warrant issued on 6-1-2003 against the present petitioner in connection with the aforesaid Special Tribunal Case No. 41 of 1996 is found to have been issued illegally and the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed therein is not in any way applicable to the present petitioner. In a case of this nature the High Court Division should always act and interfere under its inherent jurisdiction under section 561A of the Criminal Procedure Code to prevent the abuse of the process of the Court and/or otherwise to secure ends of justice and to rise on such occasion the power of the High Court Division is not in any way restricted by any law. The paramount consideration in exercising power under section 561A of the Code is that such an order will prevent abuse of the process of any court or otherwise it would secure ends of justice. Accordingly, we hold that this is a fit case where the High Court Division must not hesitate to exercise it is inherent power to prevent the abuse of the process of the court and to secure ends of justice to protect an innocent from being unnecessarily harassed and punished. 

 13. Accordingly, we are convinced that the present petitioner has been put behind the bars illegally in connection with Special Tribunal Case No. 41 of 1996 as he is not the real convict and the learned Judge of the Special Tribunal failed to appreciate this aspect and illegally rejected the present petitioner’s prayer and passed the order of issuing custody warrant on 6-1-2003 which is sheer abuse of the process of court causing failure to secure ends of justice. 

 14. Thus we find merit in this Rule and accordingly, the Rule is made absolute. The order showing arrest of the present petitioner in connection with Special Tribunal Case No. 41 of 1996 passed in NGR Case No. 124 of 2002 on 5-1-2003 and the custody warrant issued against the petitioner on 6-1-2003 by the Tribunal are found to have been passed illegally and the same are quashed. The Tribunal is directed to release the petitioner from the custody in connection with the Special Tribunal Case No. 41 of 1996 immediately, if not wanted in connection with any other case.
